name: Seven-Toed Pete Race Horse
description: Seven-Toed Pete is a fast Fives-family domino game for four players. Players score on multiples of five and gain extra turns whenever they score or play a double.

overview.description: Seven-Toed Pete is a fast Fives-family domino game for four players. Players score on multiples of five and gain extra turns whenever they score or play a double.

history.origins: Seven-Toed Pete is a U.S. Fives-family domino game. The same name has also been used for an unrelated poker game, but this entry covers the domino game only.
timeline: 2011: Rules updated with regional (East Coast vs West Coast) and spinner-handling notes.
Current: Played as a high-tempo scoring domino variant with extra-turn chains.

setup.players: Four players in the standard game; some groups also use partnership or 2-3 player variants.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 tiles; all tiles are dealt, so there is no boneyard.
setup.equipment: Domino set and score tracker (chips or score sheet).

rules.objective: Outscore opponents by making scoring plays and winning hands through domino or lowest blocked-hand pip total.
rules.gameplay: Lead is by lot in the first hand and then rotates. Opening lead must be a double or a scoring starter tile such as 0-5, 1-4, 2-3, 4-6, or 5-5; if unavailable, lead passes onward. Players match open ends or pass if blocked. Any scoring play or any double gives an immediate extra turn. If a player uses their last tile on a scoring play or double, they are washed up and play continues among others. A hand ends when a player dominoes on a non-scoring non-double play, or when the game blocks.
keyRules: Opening lead must be a double or listed scoring starter.
Any scoring play or double grants an immediate extra turn.
No boneyard in the standard four-player game.
A scoring/double final tile causes washed-up continuation, not immediate hand end.
West Coast Race Horse style often uses all doubles as spinners.

strategy.basic: Prioritize plays that score and chain extra turns.
strategy.intermediate: Use doubles tactically: they can score, branch the layout, and immediately retain initiative.
strategy.advanced: Plan around washed-up outcomes so you do not hand tempo to an opponent near domino.
tips: A fast run of scoring turns can decide a hand before opponents stabilize their ends.
Track which players still hold likely starter tiles for the next opening lead.

variations.name: West Coast Race Horse
variations.description: All doubles act as spinners; often called Race Horse or Horse Race.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant differs in spinner rule only; engine could toggle all-doubles-as-spinner via future constant.

variations.name: Chip-Win Variant
variations.description: Some groups score hand wins in chips instead of full five-based point totals.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Chip scoring is a table convention; target score and scoring display would need overrides when documented.

scoring.description: Score when exposed ends total a multiple of five. Hand winner (domino or blocked-hand low pip total) also scores opponents' remaining pips, commonly converted by dividing by five after rounding.
scoring.winCondition: Reach the table-agreed target score before opponents.

synthesis.shortDescription: Seven-Toed Pete is a rapid four-player domino game where scoring plays and doubles immediately grant extra turns.

hero.tagline: Score, chain extra turns, and race to domino.
